Explanation: A validated AI solution that addresses a concrete public-sector problem and can move from pilot toward repeatable use in other administrations.
BMDS is the public sponsor and orchestrating Owner in this PBMC; BMDS and DigitalService jointly selected the first 20 pilots and organize the Hub process.
The Owner role is to scale useful AI in administration by connecting public demand with suitable providers and creating paths beyond isolated pilots.
A successful Hub can shorten the route from identified public problem to tested solution and broaden adoption of solutions that prove transferable.
The main scaling friction appears after validation: procurement, heterogeneous local environments, infrastructure and durable operation can fragment reuse.
The Hub matches public problems with providers, creates pilot opportunities and then supports the transition toward broader adoption.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Problems — Municipalities bring concrete administrative problems and use cases into the Hub. | → Provider · Pilot — The Hub creates a matched pilot opportunity for a selected startup solution.

Explanation: Governance includes participant selection, pilot criteria, security expectations and the rules used to evaluate scalability and transferability.
The Hub and its network attract municipalities, startups and supporting stakeholders into the program and wider community.
The Owner selects, matches, coordinates and evaluates pilots and develops mechanisms for procurement and scaling.
Core resources are the public-problem pipeline, startup network, pilot evidence and the emerging procurement and scaling mechanisms.
Municipalities are the demand side of the Hub: public administrations bring concrete operational problems and test solutions in practice.
Their job is to simplify administrative work and reduce manual routine effort with usable AI solutions.
The expected gain is faster processing and relief for staff in repetitive or capacity-constrained workflows.
Municipalities face backlogs, legacy systems and limited implementation capacity when introducing new AI solutions.
They contribute concrete public problems and use cases and then test or use the resulting AI solution.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Problems — Municipalities bring concrete administrative problems and use cases into the Hub. | → Provider · Needs — After matching, municipalities provide process needs and domain context directly to the startup. | ← Provider · Solution — Startups return a working AI solution for practical testing in the municipality. | ← Partner · Service — An operating layer turns the software into a durable service that an administration can use.

Explanation: Problems are selected for public relevance, strategic fit, representativeness and potential scalability.
The Agentic AI Hub is the interface through which municipalities enter the matching and pilot process.
Municipalities apply, provide process context, test solutions with real workflows and evaluate whether they work.
They contribute use cases, domain knowledge, process context, staff time and, where appropriate, operational data.
AI startups and scale-ups form the Provider side by bringing specialist technologies and teams into the public-sector pilot process.
Their job is to turn a public-sector problem into a working AI solution that can be validated in practice.
The Hub gives providers access to public-sector demand, references and a potential path from pilot to broader adoption.
Moving from a successful pilot to repeatable public-sector business requires procurement, integration and scaling across heterogeneous administrations.
Providers build and adapt software for a concrete municipal pilot and contribute the solution into the testing process.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Pilot — The Hub creates a matched pilot opportunity for a selected startup solution. | ← Consumer · Needs — After matching, municipalities provide process needs and domain context directly to the startup. | → Consumer · Solution — Startups return a working AI solution for practical testing in the municipality. | → Partner · Software — At the scaling stage, validated software has to be integrated into secure production environments.

Explanation: Startups are selected based on solution fit, strategic relevance and the potential to scale beyond one pilot.
The Hub application and matching process connects selected providers with participating municipalities.
Providers develop, adapt and iterate their AI solution with the municipality during the pilot.
They contribute AI technology, product capability, specialist knowledge and delivery teams.

Operators represent the integration and operating capabilities needed when validated solutions move from pilots into durable public services. This is an analytical PBMC role, not an official Agentic AI Hub participant category.
Their functional job is to integrate, secure and operate AI solutions reliably in public-sector environments.
A scaling layer can create recurring integration and operating work across multiple administrations and solutions.
Operators have to bridge legacy environments, security requirements, infrastructure constraints and operational responsibility.
They turn startup software into an integrated and operated service that administrations can use beyond the pilot setting.
Transaction Flows: ← Provider · Software — At the scaling stage, validated software has to be integrated into secure production environments. | → Consumer · Service — An operating layer turns the software into a durable service that an administration can use.

Explanation: Participation depends on security, technical fit, procurement conditions and the ability to operate within public-sector requirements.
Operators enter through implementation, infrastructure and operating projects rather than through the Hub as a formal participant category.
They integrate components, connect infrastructure, harden deployments and operate services over time.
They contribute cloud or compute access, integration capability, operations tooling, security know-how and service-management capacity.
